extraction_rules.alias: Within one enum, later members sharing the first-seen value are aliases of that first name. Colliding #define values across opcode classes are independent records, never aliases.
extraction_rules.callable: A helper or kfunc entry is callable only with a kernel registration reference; BTF symbol presence alone never qualifies a call.
extraction_rules.context_only: Values carried inside calls and buffers own no record but must reference at least one record.
extraction_rules.flag: Settable option words own flag records in the family they qualify.
extraction_rules.registration: Helper callability derives from case labels in get_func_proto callback bodies reachable from a program type's verifier-ops root; kfunc membership derives from ID blocks referenced by a btf_kfunc_id_set and program bindings derive from register calls through the pinned btf.c hook switch. Hook, allowlist and fmodret attach-target sets never qualify a call. Registration .filter callbacks narrow kfunc callability per member and version; an always-denying filter leaves no callable context. struct_ops consumer and sched_ext endpoint registrations enumerate from struct bpf_struct_ops definitions, and every sched_ext operations-table callback owns a record.
extraction_rules.selftests: Every pinned *.c selftest ID maps onto exactly one capability record, or is cited as blocker evidence; unmapped IDs abort generation.
extraction_rules.sentinel: UNSPEC members, __MAX sentinels and count sentinels are reserved, never capabilities.
traversal: Parse every enumerator, object-like and function-like define, helper-mapper entry, symbol-map entry, section-table entry and toolchain fact in the staged sources.
Struct and union members are not enumerated; option records are covered through the library API surface.
extraction_rules.union: The registry is the union of the pinned UAPI versions; each atom records every version that provides it. Value or shape conflicts across versions abort generation.
extraction_rules.unknown: Any atom without a classification rule aborts generation until it is assigned an owner and tests.
